title_en: Supreme People's Court's Nine Typical Cases on Anti-Avoidance of Enforcement
full_text_en:
1. Capital Normal University v. Zhongjian Property Management Company — enforcement of judgment for dispute over heat supply contract

Summary of Facts

In the case of dispute over heat supply contract between Capital Normal University and Zhongjian Property Management Company, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing rendered a judgment ordering Zhongjian Property Management Company to pay Capital Normal University heating fees of RMB 2,913,715.7 and interest of RMB 270,025.17. After the first-instance judgment, Zhongjian Property Management Company appealed. The Beijing No.1 Intermediate People's Court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original judgment in the second instance.

Since Zhongjian Property Management Company failed to perform the obligations determined by the effective judgment, Capital Normal University applied to the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing for enforcement. The enforcement court ordered Zhongjian Property Management Company to report its property situation. Zhongjian Property Management Company reported two bank accounts at Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and China Merchants Bank. The enforcement court froze both accounts and only deducted RMB 9,800. Further investigation by the enforcement court revealed that Zhongjian Property Management Company also had an account at China Construction Bank, which the enforcement court froze, with a deposit of only RMB 13,289.02. The enforcement court required the person in charge of Zhongjian Property Management Company to appear in court to explain why it had not truthfully reported its property, and also required Zhongjian Property Management Company to provide bank statements and accounting vouchers for the three accounts for investigation. The person in charge of Zhongjian Property Management Company did not appear in court and failed to provide the bank statements and accounting vouchers. In light of this, the enforcement court searched the office premises of Zhongjian Property Management Company. By reviewing the accounting ledgers obtained from the search, it was discovered that Zhongjian Property Management Company had made large payments to the Zhongjian North Annex Building Guesthouse under the names of wages, medicine expenses, travel expenses, etc., totaling nearly one million yuan. The enforcement court obtained transaction records of Zhongjian Property Management Company's China Construction Bank account, which showed that even after the enforcement court issued the enforcement notice, Zhongjian Property Management Company still had multiple large-sum fund transfers. The enforcement court investigated the business premises of the Zhongjian North Annex Building Guesthouse and found that the guesthouse was very rudimentary, with only six employees and monthly operating income of RMB 20,000 to 30,000.

After investigation, the enforcement court obtained a large amount of solid evidence proving that after receiving the enforcement notice, Zhongjian Property Management Company failed to truthfully report its property situation and transferred large sums of money such as operating income to the bank account of the Zhongjian North Annex Building Guesthouse in order to transfer property and evade enforcement. Therefore, the enforcement court took detention measures against the person in charge of Zhongjian Property Management Company and decided to audit the accounts of Zhongjian Property Management Company. After the enforcement court took compulsory measures, Zhongjian Property Management Company, under pressure, paid over RMB 1.8 million in enforcement funds to the court within three days and entered into an enforcement settlement agreement with the applicant Capital Normal University, which has been fully performed in installments.

Typical Significance

The enforcement court strictly implemented the property reporting system, intensified ex officio investigation of property, and appropriately used auditing methods to investigate the property of the person subject to enforcement, thereby enabling the smooth conclusion of the case.

2. Zhang Qu v. Chen Shi and Wu Yangying — enforcement of judgment for private lending dispute

Summary of Facts

In the case of dispute over private lending between Zhang Qu and Chen Shi and Wu Yangying, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province rendered a judgment ordering Chen Shi to repay Zhang Qu RMB 1.88 million plus interest, and defendant Wu Yangying to bear joint and several liability for compensation. After the first-instance judgment, Chen Shi and Wu Yangying appealed. The Fujian High People's Court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original judgment in the second instance.

Since Chen Shi and Wu Yangying failed to perform the obligations determined by the effective judgment, Zhang Qu applied to the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court for compulsory enforcement. The enforcement court decided to compulsorily auction the property located at No. 02, First Floor, Building 5, Fuzhou Xinhuijiayuan, No. 136 Fubei North Road, Xindian Town, Jin'an District, Fuzhou, which was under the name of Wu Yangying and had been sealed up for preservation during the litigation phase. The person subject to enforcement, Wu Yangying, presented to the court a lease contract she had signed with her younger brother concerning the above property, which stipulated a monthly rent of RMB 950, a lease term of 15 years, and rent paid in a lump sum. Wu Yangying claimed that before the court sealed the property, she had already leased it to her younger brother and received a one-time rent of RMB 170,000. After signing the contract, her younger brother subleased the property to a third party (the sub-lessee). Wu Yangying was unable to provide relevant transfer vouchers from financial institutions proving that she had received the RMB 170,000 rent in one lump sum. In response, Wu Yangying argued that she had borrowed money from her younger brother to purchase the property and agreed to use the rent from the property to repay the loan. The applicant Zhang Qu submitted a report to the enforcement court, stating that she had personally seen Wu Yangying collecting rent from the sub-lessee and believed that the lease contract presented by Wu Yangying was forged through collusion between Wu Yangying and her brother. The enforcement personnel investigated the matter with several persons who had been lessees of the property; these lessees confirmed that Wu Yanging collected rent each month, with a monthly rent of RMB 3,000. After obtaining sufficient evidence, the enforcement personnel interviewed Wu Yangying's younger brother. Wu Yangying's younger brother admitted that after Wu Yangying learned that the property had been sealed by the court, she subleased the property to the sub-lessee in his name. The signatures on the sublease contract were made by Wu Yangying, and Wu Yangying directly collected rent from the sub-lessee.

The enforcement court held that the lease relationship on the sealed property did not affect the disposal of the sealed property. The enforcement court decided to auction the sealed property and informed the person subject to enforcement in the auction announcement that she had the right to raise an objection. Wu Yangying did not raise an objection within the prescribed time limit. Before the court decided to compulsorily auction the property, Wu Yangying's younger brother voluntarily withdrew from the tripartite lease and sublease relationship. The enforcement court appraised and auctioned the property in accordance with the law. After the auction was concluded, the original sub-lessee still enjoyed the lease rights and paid rent to the buyer instead.

Typical Significance

The people's court strengthened property preservation measures and intensified enforcement efforts against preserved property, thereby enabling the smooth execution of the case.

3. Shanghai Jindi Petrochemical Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Liyu Trading Co., Ltd. — enforcement of judgment for tort damages dispute

Summary of Facts

In the case of dispute over tort damages between Shanghai Jindi Petrochemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jindi Company) and Shanghai Liyu Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Liyu Company), the Shanghai High People's Court issued a civil mediation letter confirming that Liyu Company should pay Jindi Company RMB 8.8 million, and Yang Liping should bear joint and several liability for Liyu Company's payment obligation within the scope of RMB 7.4 million.

Liyu Company and Yang Liping failed to perform the payment obligation stipulated in the mediation letter. Jindi Company applied to the Shanghai No.1 Intermediate People's Court, the court of first instance, for compulsory enforcement. The enforcement court found that Liyu Company, due to involvement in a criminal case, had been determined by relevant institutions to be insolvent. Yang Liping originally owned four properties, but two days before Jindi Company filed the lawsuit, Yang Liping signed three "Shanghai Real Estate Sales Contracts" with Gong Mou (Yang Liping's son), "selling" three of her four properties to Gong Mou, and subsequently completed the property transfer procedures.

After enforcement was filed, Jindi Company filed a lawsuit with the Minhang District People's Court of Shanghai to revoke the real estate sales contracts between Yang Liping and Gong Mou. The Shanghai No.1 Intermediate People's Court then ruled to suspend the enforcement of the case. The Minhang District People's Court of Shanghai found during the trial that Yang Liping was a shareholder of Liyu Company. When interrogated by the public security authorities, she clearly stated that Gong Mou had not actually paid the purchase price. Gong Mou was only 20 years old at the time of the property transfer, was studying abroad, and relied on his parents for living expenses, lacking the ability to pay the purchase price. The court held that Yang Liping, foreseeing the possibility of being held liable, transferred her property ownership to Gong Mou without compensation, with subjective intent to evade debts, and this effectively reduced her ability to repay debts, harming the interests of creditors. Therefore, the court revoked the three "Shanghai Real Estate Sales Contracts" signed by Yang Liping and Gong Mou. Subsequently, Jindi Company applied for restoration of enforcement, requesting the disposal of the properties that had been restored to Yang Liping's name. After the enforcement court restored the enforcement, Jindi Company and Yang Liping entered into a settlement agreement: Yang Liping transferred one of her properties to Jindi Company and compensated Jindi Company RMB 160,000, while Jindi Company waived its other claims. The case was concluded.

Typical Significance

Where a person subject to enforcement transfers property without compensation, causing harm to the applicant for enforcement, the applicant may file a revocation action with the competent people's court in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract Law, effectively counteracting evasion of enforcement.

4. Hubei Hongxin Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. and Tuanfeng County Fanggaoping Construction Company v. Yiyuan Keda Magnetic Materials Co., Ltd. and Huanggang Zhongji Automobile Sales Co., Ltd. — enforcement of judgment for project payment guarantee dispute

Summary of Facts

In the case of enforcement of a dispute over project payment guarantee between Hubei Hongxin Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongxin Company), Tuanfeng County Fanggaoping Construction Company (hereinafter referred to as Fanggaoping Construction Company), and Yiyuan Keda Magnetic Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yiyuan Company) and Huanggang Zhongji Automobile Sales Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongji Company), the Huanggang Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province filed the case for enforcement on March 3, 2008. Yiyuan Company refused to perform the obligations determined by the effective judgment on the grounds that its legal representative, Ding Mou, was a member of the Municipal Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) and that the company had no ability to repay. Through investigation, the enforcement court found that several bank accounts that Yiyuan Company had registered with the People's Bank of China each had deposits ranging from a few yuan to a few hundred yuan; the company's immovable property had been mortgaged, and there was no other property available for enforcement; Zhongji Company had already ceased operations and had no property available for enforcement. On May 19, 2008, the applicant for enforcement provided clues to the enforcement court that Yiyuan Company had received a payment of RMB 750,000 remitted from Shenzhen. The enforcement personnel immediately checked the several bank accounts Yiyuan Company had registered with the People's Bank of China, but did not find the remittance. Subsequently, the enforcement personnel discovered an account Yiyuan Company had opened with Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (which was not registered with the People's Bank of China), located the remittance, but the funds had already been transferred out. Investigation revealed that the funds were transferred to the personal account of Yiyuan Company's accountant, Deng Mou, on the same day the remittance arrived. Based on the above, the enforcement court believed that Yiyuan Company was suspected of concealing assets and evading enforcement, and immediately froze the RMB 650,000 deposit in Deng Mou's personal account. Deng Mou raised an objection to the enforcement, claiming that the funds in the frozen account were a loan repaid by Yiyuan Company to him, constituting his personal property. The enforcement court examined the objection in accordance with the law. After comparing the accounts of Yiyuan Company and Deng Mou, it was found that from November 2007 to May 2008, all large-sum funds (22 transactions totaling RMB 1.565 million) entering Yiyuan Company's account were transferred to Deng Mou's personal account on the day of or the day after receipt. Deng Mou's personal account had no other deposit records apart from the 22 transfers from the company account. During the review, Deng Mou presented an IOU with Yiyuan Company's seal, showing an amount of RMB 860,000. However, upon investigation of Yiyuan Company's accounting books, no record of this loan was found. The enforcement court found that Deng Mou was over 50 years old, a laid-off worker, his spouse was unemployed, and the family was financially strained. Based on this, the court inferred that the lending relationship between Deng Mou and Yiyuan Company was inconsistent with common sense. The enforcement court required Deng Mou to explain the source of the funds and the method of payment, and warned him of the legal consequences of false statements. Deng Mou gave vague responses and voluntarily requested to withdraw the IOU. Based on the facts found during the review, the enforcement court determined that Yiyuan Company was the actual owner of the funds in Deng Mou's account and lawfully ruled to reject Deng Mou's objection. After signing the ruling, Deng Mou filed an objection lawsuit with the enforcement court, but later withdrew the lawsuit before the trial.

The enforcement court imposed a fine on Yiyuan Company for intentionally concealing assets and obstructing enforcement, and also, with the consent and support of the Huanggang Municipal Committee of the CPPCC, detained Ding Mou, the legal representative of Yiyuan Company. Neither Yiyuan Company nor Ding Mou raised any objection, appealed, or petitioned. The case was successfully enforced.

Typical Significance

Where a person subject to enforcement makes a false property report, fabricates debts, or conceals or transfers property, causing loss to the applicant for enforcement, the enforcement court may impose fines and detention on the person subject to enforcement and its relevant responsible persons in accordance with the law, thereby enabling the smooth conclusion of the case.

5. Guangdong Huidong County Construction Engineering Corporation v. Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd. — enforcement of judgment for project payment dispute

Summary of Facts

In the case of enforcement of a dispute over project payment between Guangdong Huidong County Construction Engineering Corporation and Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd., the Huidong County People's Court of Guangdong Province issued an enforcement notice and a property reporting order to the person subject to enforcement, Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd., on January 13, 2010, ordering the person subject to enforcement to pay RMB 800,000 in project payments to the applicant for enforcement by January 20 of the same year. After receiving the enforcement notice, the person subject to enforcement, Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd., sent a representative to appear in court, but did not report the company's property situation and expressed a desire to settle the case by having the applicant spend RMB 300,000 at a designated hotel. Upon investigation, the enforcement court found that the person subject to enforcement, Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd., was a Hong Kong-invested enterprise, its legal representative, Li Yousheng, was a Hong Kong resident, the company's bank deposits were only a little over RMB 1,000, and the real estate registered under the company's name, covering a total area of 16,357 square meters, had been mortgaged to a bank. Furthermore, the real estate had been leased by Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd. to a hotel for a lease term of 60 years, with rent collected in one lump sum by the person subject to enforcement, rendering the property unable to be disposed of and converted into cash.

Because the legal representative of the person subject to enforcement, Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd., Li Yousheng, was a Hong Kong resident, the enforcement court decided to impose a restriction on his exit from the country. On the evening of March 25, 2010, Li Yousheng, who was preparing to exit the country at the Shenzhen Luohu port, was restricted from leaving. Subsequently, the enforcement court decided to detain him. After being detained, Li Yousheng voluntarily admitted his mistakes in failing to report property and failing to perform the obligations specified in the legal document. Ultimately, the applicant for enforcement, Guangdong Huidong County Construction Engineering Corporation, and the person subject to enforcement, Master Trade Mart (Huidong) Co., Ltd., entered into an enforcement settlement agreement, and the person subject to enforcement paid the full RMB 800,000 in project payments to the applicant for enforcement in two installments.

Typical Significance

Because the person subject to enforcement failed to perform the obligations specified in the legal document, the enforcement court lawfully imposed measures restricting exit from the country and detention on the legal representative of the person subject to enforcement. Under the powerful legal deterrence, the person subject to enforcement performed its obligations, and the case was successfully concluded.

6. Zhou Mingli: Refusal to Enforce Judgment or Ruling

Summary of Facts

Defendant: Zhou Mingli, male, Han ethnicity, born on April 6, 1972, in Dangshan County, Anhui Province, junior high school education, farmer, residing at Tundian Village, Yongfeng Township, Haidian District, Beijing, before arrest.

On July 20, 2007, the defendant Zhou Mingli, while driving a Geely passenger car (license plate number Jing HQ4771) at the intersection of Taizhouwu East Road Brick Factory in Haidian District, Beijing, collided with a pedestrian, Sun Ailong, causing injury. The traffic management department determined that Zhou Mingli bore full responsibility for the accident. Subsequently, Sun Ailong filed a lawsuit against Zhou Mingli in the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing. On June 18, 2008, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing rendered a judgment ordering Zhou Mingli to compensate Sun Ailong RMB 43,398.26.

During the period after the above judgment became effective, Zhou Mingli received accident compensation of RMB 62,872.3 from Anbang Property Insurance Co., Ltd., but instead of fulfilling his compensation obligation to Sun Ailong, he misappropriated the funds for other purposes. After learning that Sun Ailong had applied for enforcement, he also transferred the Geely passenger car to another person's name. On August 15, 2008, after being summoned to the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, Zhou Mingli truthfully confessed to transferring property to evade enforcement. On the same day, Zhou Mingli was placed under judicial detention by the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing and subsequently transferred to the public security authorities.

The Haidian District People's Procuratorate of Beijing filed a public prosecution with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, charging Zhou Mingli with the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling. After trial, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing found that the defendant Zhou Mingli, while having the ability to enforce the people's court's judgment, transferred property to refuse enforcement, with serious circumstances. His conduct constituted the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling. Given that Zhou Mingli voluntarily surrendered after being summoned by telephone and truthfully confessed his crime, constituting voluntary surrender, and combined with his good attitude of admitting guilt and having performed the compensation obligation determined by the civil judgment after being subjected to criminal prosecution, he could be given a lighter punishment. Accordingly, the court sentenced the defendant Zhou Mingli to eight months' imprisonment for the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling.

Typical Significance

After causing a traffic accident, Zhou Mingli received insurance compensation specifically for compensating third-party economic losses caused by the accident from the insurance company, but instead of paying it to the victim, he misappropriated it for other purposes and transferred the vehicle to a non-party, making the effective judgment unenforceable. His refusal to enforce the judgment was punished by criminal sanctions. The handling of this case serves as a good educational and exemplary effect on the current practice where obligors in traffic accident damages cases misappropriate motor vehicle insurance compensation and transfer or conceal motor vehicles to evade enforcement, and possesses certain typical significance.

7. Li Yonghui: Refusal to Enforce Judgment or Ruling

Summary of Facts

Defendant: Li Yonghui, male, Han ethnicity, born on July 30, 1964, in Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, college education, legal representative of Xinjiang Xiehe Natural Products Co., Ltd., residing at Room 402, Unit 2, Building 32, Xingfu Garden, Urumqi City, before arrest.

On April 20, 2007, the Bortala Mongolian Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rendered judgments in two cases brought by the plaintiff Xinjiang Huaye International Trade Co., Ltd. against the defendant Xinjiang Xiehe Natural Products Co., Ltd. and Li Yonghui, involving disputes over sales contracts and agency contracts, ordering Xinjiang Xiehe Natural Products Co., Ltd. to repay Xinjiang Huaye International Trade Co., Ltd. a total of over RMB 9 million in goods prices and interest, with Li Yonghui bearing joint and several liability personally. After the judgments became effective and entered the enforcement phase, the Bortala Mongolian Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court lawfully served an enforcement notice on Li Yonghui. Instead of performing the obligation, Li Yonghui transferred and hid the vehicles that had been seized by the Bortala Mongolian Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court on April 11, 2007 (Jianghuai passenger bus, license plate New A-92691; Fukang car, license plate New AC-3362) and on August 24, 2007 (Santana sedan, license plate New A67700) to places such as Hangzhou City in Zhejiang Province. He also went into hiding in places such as Hangzhou City, deactivated his original mobile phone number, thereby rendering the judgment unenforceable.

In January 2008, Li Yonghui was placed under judicial detention by the Bortala Mongolian Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court and subsequently transferred to the public security authorities. In November of the same year, the Bole City People's Procuratorate of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region filed a public prosecution with the Bole City People's Court, charging Li Yonghui with the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling.

Bole City People's Court found after trial that the defendant Li Yonghui ignored the effective judgment of the court, had the ability to perform but refused to perform the payment obligations determined by the judgment, and took measures such as transferring and concealing the property seized by the court, deactivating his mobile phone number, and hiding in another place to evade enforcement by the court. The circumstances were serious, and his conduct constituted the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling. Accordingly, he was sentenced to two years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment. After the judgment was pronounced, Li Yonghui appealed. The Intermediate People's Court of Bortala Mongolian Autonomous Prefecture found after trial that the original judgment had clear facts, reliable and sufficient evidence, correct characterization, proper application of law, and appropriate sentencing, and ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

【Typical Significance】The person subject to execution, Li Yonghui, hid and transferred property that had been sealed up during the execution process, causing the judgment to be unenforceable. According to the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court, this constitutes "serious circumstances" of the act of refusing to enforce a people's court's judgment or ruling, and criminal liability for the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling should be pursued in accordance with the law. The handling of this case serves an educational and promotional role in combating, in accordance with the law, the illegal acts of some persons subject to execution who, during practice, arbitrarily hide, transfer, sell, or damage property that has been legally sealed up, seized, or inventoried and ordered to be kept in their custody.

8. Chen Shaohuan and Hong Guicheng — case of refusal to enforce a judgment or ruling

【Case Summary】Defendant Chen Shaohuan, female, Han ethnicity, born on February 2, 1969, with elementary school education, farmer. Defendant Hong Guicheng, male, Han ethnicity, born on December 16, 1965, with elementary school education, resident. The two are husband and wife, residing at No. 15, East Third Lane, Hongqiaotou, Songgang Town, Baoan District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province before arrest.

On April 3, 2008, Jian'ou City People's Court, Fujian Province rendered a judgment in the case of plaintiff Jian'ou Liwei Plastic Co., Ltd. v. defendants Shenzhen Deyang Plastic and Bakelite Co., Ltd., Chen Shaohuan, and Hong Guicheng concerning a dispute over a sales contract, ordering Shenzhen Deyang Plastic and Bakelite Co., Ltd. to pay Jian'ou Liwei Plastic Co., Ltd. RMB 509,250 for the goods and liquidated damages, and ordering Chen Shaohuan and Hong Guicheng to personally assume guarantee liability for the above debt.

After the judgment became effective, the couple Chen Shaohuan and Hong Guicheng sold the property under their names located at No. 18, San Xiang, Yicun New District, Tangxiachong Community, Songgang Street, Baoan District, Shenzhen City on May 8, 2008, for RMB 2.2 million; in July of the same year, they also sold the machinery and equipment of Shenzhen Deyang Plastic and Bakelite Co., Ltd. for RMB 115,000. They did not use the proceeds to perform the debts determined by the effective judgment, but transferred the funds elsewhere, causing the court judgment to be unenforceable.

On April 8, 2009, Chen Shaohuan was criminally detained by the public security organs of Jian'ou City; on April 27 of the same month, Hong Guicheng voluntarily surrendered. After the incident, the two defendants reached a settlement agreement with the application enforcement applicant, Jian'ou Liwei Plastic Co., Ltd., and performed it in full in June of the same year.

After Jian'ou City People's Procuratorate, Fujian Province instituted a public prosecution on charges that Chen Shaohuan and Hong Guicheng were suspected of committing the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling, Jian'ou City People's Court found after trial that, under circumstances where the civil judgment of the court had already taken legal effect, defendants Chen Shaohuan and Hong Guicheng, for the purpose of evading debts, intentionally sold and transferred performable property, causing the court judgment to be unenforceable. The circumstances were serious, and their conduct constituted the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling. Considering that the two had good attitudes in confessing after the incident and fully performed their obligations, and that Hong Guicheng also had the circumstance of voluntary surrender, they could be given lighter punishments separately. Accordingly, for the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling, Chen Shaohuan was sentenced to two years of fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for three years; Hong Guicheng was sentenced to one year and six months of fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for two years.

【Typical Significance】In practice, persons subject to execution resort to every possible means to transfer or conceal property in order to evade performing obligations determined by effective judgments. A common method is to sell or dispose of property under their own names. Such conduct must be severely sanctioned. In this case, after the judgment became effective, the couple who were the persons subject to execution sold the house and transferred the proceeds from the sale, which clearly constituted having the ability to perform but refusing to do so, and criminal liability should be pursued in accordance with the law. Moreover, this case also illustrates from another perspective that for those persons subject to execution suspected of committing the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling, as long as they recognize the situation, voluntarily surrender, and actively perform their obligations, they may receive a lighter punishment in accordance with the criminal policy of combining leniency with severity.

9. Li Yongming and Ding Zheliang (person subject to execution) — case of false litigation

【Case Summary】Defendant Li Yongming, male, Han ethnicity, born on September 22, 1971 in Shengzhou City, Zhejiang Province, with junior high school education, unemployed. Previously, he was sentenced to three years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment for robbery in August 1994, and was released upon completion of the sentence in August 1997.

Defendant Ding Zheliang, male, Han ethnicity, born on June 28, 1977 in Shengzhou City, Zhejiang Province, with junior high school education, farmer, residing at No. 60, Wanglongwan, Fukengkou Village, Chongren Town, Shengzhou City before arrest.

In September 2007, due to economic disputes with others, Ding Zheliang's property located at Room 501, Unit 2, Building 15, East Garden, Jinxiujiayuan, No. 877 Xianhu Road, Shengzhou City was sealed up by Shengzhou City People's Court. In 2008, Shengzhou City People's Court successively accepted four cases with Ding Zheliang as the person subject to execution, with total claim amount of over RMB 1.4 million. In November of the same year, Ding Zheliang's sealed property was auctioned for RMB 370,000.

In 2006, due to business needs, Ding Zheliang borrowed a total of RMB 100,000 from Li Yongming. In December 2007, Li Yongming instructed Ding Zheliang to forge a house lease contract with him, stipulating that the above house would be leased for RMB 100,000 for a term of 20 years, with the signing date being June 2007, before the property was sealed up. In February 2008, in order to obtain a larger share of the debt interests, Li Yongming further instructed Ding Zheliang to forge with him an IOU showing that Ding Zheliang borrowed RMB 350,000 from him, and in March of the same year filed a lawsuit with Shengzhou City People's Court. Before the trial, both parties reached a mediation agreement on repayment, which was confirmed by Shengzhou City People's Court through Civil Mediation Paper No. (2008) Sheng Min Er Chu Zi No. 592.

Li Yongming applied for enforcement based on the aforementioned civil mediation paper from Shengzhou City People's Court, requesting to participate in the distribution, and on the ground that he had already paid the full amount of RMB 100,000 in rent to Ding Zheliang in one lump sum, requested that the court first refund the remaining house rental fees. When multiple creditors lawfully received repayment from the auction proceeds of Ding Zheliang's property, they raised objections to the IOU between Li Yongming and the person subject to execution, Ding Zheliang. Shengzhou City People's Court investigated and found that Li Yongming and Ding Zheliang had engaged in false litigation by fabricating debts. Therefore, on April 29, 2009, the court decided to retry the case, and on July 15, 2009, rendered a judgment revoking the original civil mediation paper. Thereafter, Shengzhou City People's Court transferred the leads regarding Li Yongming and Ding Zheliang's suspected crime of false litigation to the public security organs for case filing and investigation. On November 12, 2009, Li Yongming and Ding Zheliang voluntarily surrendered to Shengzhou City Public Security Bureau.

On April 9, 2010, Shengzhou City People's Procuratorate instituted a public prosecution against Li Yongming and Ding Zheliang on charges of suspected obstruction of testimony and assisting in forging evidence, respectively. After trial, Shengzhou City People's Court held that defendant Li Yongming, in order to obtain a larger share of debt interests, instructed another person to forge an IOU, filed a lawsuit with the people's court and applied for enforcement, which seriously obstructed the normal litigation activities of the judicial organs. His conduct constituted the crime of obstruction of testimony. Defendant Ding Zheliang, in order to enable Li Yongming to obtain a larger share of debt interests, assisted him in forging an IOU. The circumstances were serious, and his conduct constituted the crime of assisting in forging evidence. In view of the fact that both voluntarily surrendered after committing the crimes and truthfully confessed their own crimes, which constitute voluntary surrender, they could both be given lighter punishments. Accordingly, Li Yongming was sentenced to one year of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of obstruction of testimony, and Ding Zheliang was sentenced to eight months of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of assisting in forging evidence.

【Typical Significance】In judicial practice, situations occasionally occur where a debtor colludes with individual creditors or persons not involved in the case to engage in false litigation, asserting claims over the debtor's property and infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of other creditors. Such conduct must be resolutely combated in accordance with the law. In this case, creditor Li Yongming, in order to obtain a larger share of debt interests, instructed debtor Ding Zheliang to forge an IOU showing that Ding Zheliang borrowed RMB 350,000 from him. After filing a lawsuit with the court, it was confirmed by a civil mediation paper, and based on this, Li Yongming applied for participating in the distribution, resulting in reduced amounts for other creditors and infringement upon the lawful rights and interests of others. After the incident, the people's court, based on the facts found, convicted and sentenced Li Yongming and Ding Zheliang for the crimes of obstruction of testimony and assisting in forging evidence, respectively, which was accurate and appropriate. The handling of this case serves as a warning to relevant parties: engaging in false litigation where the circumstances are serious will result in criminal liability being pursued in accordance with the law.
